app.title: LQL-Equiv 3.0 — Equivalent doses in radiotherapy
app.summary: A person picks an organ at risk and a tumour site from a built-in parameter library, sets the reference fraction size and model options, and enters one or more successive treatment courses as dose per fraction, number of fractions and the gap before each course. The interface computes equivalent doses for both tissues, complication and control probabilities, and a per-course table. It can also show a range for each result when the α/β ratio is varied. The person then varies the last course along a curve, or checks which fraction size best spares one tissue while holding the effect on the other fixed. Finally they save named scenarios to a comparison table and download it as CSV or JSON.

task.text: Convert treatment schedules into biologically equivalent doses for a target and an organ at risk, so schedules with different fractionation can be compared and the alternatives exported.

data.text: A prescription made of successive courses, each with a dose per fraction, a fraction count and a preceding gap, evaluated against a fixed library of tissue parameters; the computed results are tables of doses and probabilities.
data.item: a treatment schedule (one or more courses) evaluated for one organ and one target tissue

stage.text: designing and comparing fractionation schedules before a protocol is settled

mechanism.text: Sidebar choices and course inputs feed one model computation that fills summary metrics and a per-course table. Tabs then sweep the last course to draw isoeffect curves with optional α/β uncertainty bands, plot a therapeutic window that holds one tissue's effect fixed and highlights the best fraction size, and gather saved scenarios into a table for export.

field.text: biologically equivalent dose modelling (linear-quadratic-linear) in radiation oncology

workflow.name: compute model outputs for alternative input scenarios and compare them

steps.step: choose the model and its parameters
steps.here: Select an organ at risk and a tumour site from the tissue library, then set the reference dose per fraction, two fractions a day, the TCP sigmoid (logistic or Poisson) and slider or typed entry; the tabulated parameters and their models can be expanded
Set the number of successive courses; each course takes a dose per fraction, a fraction count and the treatment days missed before it, and shows its total physical dose

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Metrics show the equivalent dose for the organ and the target, NTCP and TCP, with a per-course table of overall time, BED and EQD. An optional α/β ±% spread adds a range

steps.step: vary one input and see how the result responds
steps.here: Isoeffect tab sweeps the last course's fraction count or dose per fraction and draws the cumulative equivalent dose for both tissues, with the entered schedule marked and optional α/β bands

Therapeutic-window tab holds the target (or organ) effect fixed, solves whole-fraction schedules at each fraction size, and plots the other tissue's dose with α/β bars. The best point is named only when its uncertainty clears all the others
Save the current schedule as a named scenario into a session table of doses, NTCP and TCP, then download it as CSV or JSON or clear it

distinctive: two tissues are evaluated together, the tumour and an organ at risk, each with its own proliferation model
successive courses are added up in order, each with its own gap, and only the last course is varied, because the earlier ones count as already delivered
parameter uncertainty is shown as a band from varying α/β by a chosen percentage, and a 'best' schedule is claimed only when its band clears every other
results past the model's range are flagged as bounds rather than solutions, and invalid combinations are reported as not computable
